title: Miles 101
subtitle: Reinforcement learning on language models with Miles, from one GPU to a run you can trust
summary: How to run GRPO with Miles on one GPU, choose a model that fits, and check that the run is correct. Every measured line comes from recorded runs on a DGX Spark.

plate.title: One GRPO step on one GB10
plate.caption: The SGLang engine and the FSDP trainer take turns on the Blackwell GPU. The one that waits stays parked in the same 128 GB pool. Medians of 48 steps on one GB10, from a run made before we added the heat guard.

audience: You can serve a model and you know what a reward is. You want to train a model with reinforcement learning, and you want to know which settings matter before you rent a cluster.
outcomes: Run GRPO on one GPU with the radixark/miles image and read the first ten steps.
Stop a run that keeps going after its rollout engine died.
Pick a model size that fits training and rollout on one GPU.
Check that a run is correct, and not only that it runs.
Find the cause of a failed run from its first symptom.

palette.meaning: the trainer: the FSDP actor, its weights, and its optimizer
the rollout engine: the SGLang server that generates samples
data and rewards: prompts, samples, groups, and scores
lifecycle: steps, phases, and weight versions
durable state: checkpoints, logs, and the summary files
failure: a dead engine, an out-of-memory kill, a crash
outside Miles: the host, Docker, and Ray

parts.title: Start
parts.thesis: One GRPO step on your own GPU, a watchdog that stops a dead run, and the ten steps that tell you the run is healthy.
parts.summary: Install, run, guard, and read a first run.

parts.title: Size it
parts.thesis: Training and rollout share one GPU, so the model you can train is the model whose two copies fit together.
parts.summary: Model size, offload choices, Ray on unified memory, and the cost of a weight update.

parts.title: Recipes
parts.thesis: Each recipe gives the flags to set, the flags to leave alone, and the metric that proves the run works.
parts.summary: Math, DAPO, agents, MoE, and custom rewards.

parts.title: Speed and stability
parts.thesis: Every speed or stability feature has a cost, and each page says when the cost is worth it.
parts.summary: Async, partial rollout, FP8 rollout, replay, determinism, and true on-policy.

parts.title: Check your run
parts.thesis: A run can finish every step and still train the wrong thing, so check the signals before you trust the reward.
parts.summary: The signals, the step-0 checks, and seed spread.

parts.title: Scale out
parts.thesis: Miles is built for many GPUs, and this part says which choices you make there and which we could not measure on one GPU.

parts.title: Debug
parts.thesis: Start from the symptom you see, and each entry gives the cause, the check, and the fix.
parts.summary: Troubleshooting by symptom, and records that make runs comparable.

parts.title: How Miles works
parts.thesis: This optional part explains why Miles is built the way it is, for readers who want the reasons behind the settings.
parts.summary: Mismatch, correction methods, memory, plugins, routing, and history.

reference.title: Reference
reference.thesis: The flags, metrics, lab notes, and sources this manual uses, in one place.
